arguments.value: BCDEdit can enumerate BCD stores it can access, but it does not magically manage every connected drive automatically. `bcdedit /enum all` can show entries from the currently active system BCD store and any stores you explicitly point it to, which is why you may see boot data related to multiple disks or partitions. In UEFI systems, the firmware can boot from an EFI System Partition on any connected drive, but Windows typically uses one active BCD store at a time. If you need to inspect or edit a specific drive’s BCD, you usually mount that EFI partition and target its BCD store directly.
